verdict.rationale: OpenTofu's manifesto says the project is part of the Linux Foundation, which provides neutral governance. It promises the project will stay 'truly open source' under a widely accepted license 'that won't suddenly change in the future', which addresses the relicensing concern directly. The evidence is only first-party manifesto claims and does not show the governance structure or the specific license, so coverage is partial. Community criticism that maintainers act like owners is general skepticism, not a concrete counter-example. missing for 10: the specific license named in the evidence, documentation of the governance model (steering committee, contributor rules, foundation charter preventing relicensing), and independent corroboration of the governance guarantees.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can rely on an open license and open governance so the tool cannot be relicensed out from under my company

citations.quote: Now that we are part of the Linux Foundation, we can guarantee that OpenTofu will remain: Truly open source
Truly open source - under a well-known and widely-accepted license that companies can trust, that won't suddenly change in the future
